title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary: The school nurse provides a flowchart to help distinguish between allergy symptoms and cold symptoms. **Key differences**: Allergies typically involve clear mucus, seasonal occurrence, itchiness, and symptoms that last for extended periods. Colds usually present with green or yellow mucus, fever, body discomfort, and symptoms that come on quickly and taper off fairly rapidly. **Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, symptoms worsen or new symptoms develop, you have a sore throat or fever higher than 100 degrees for longer than three days, or you experience intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

title: Allergies or Cold: Know the Difference
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary:
The school nurse provides a diagnostic flowchart to help distinguish between allergies and a cold. Key differentiators include:
- **Mucus color**: Clear mucus suggests allergies; green or yellow suggests a cold
- **Symptom duration**: Seasonal or extended symptoms indicate allergies; quick onset and resolution suggests a cold
- **Itchiness**: Itchy eyes, nose, and throat are more common with allergies
- **Fever**: Having a fever points toward a cold rather than allergies

**Call your doctor if** symptoms last longer than two weeks, worsen, include sore throat/fever over 100°F for more than three days, or involve intense chest pain and shortness of breath.

title: The Parent Project Program for Parents and Teens
source_title: Bogan Weekly News | Smore Newsletters for Education
summary: **The Parent Project** is a free 10-week program for Butler County residents that empowers parents and transforms teens through the Why Try Program. The program runs **Tuesdays, April 14 - June 16, 6pm-8pm via Zoom** and helps parents learn to never argue with teens, prevent/intervene in alcohol or drug use, improve school attendance and performance, and explore solutions for media issues. The program uses visual metaphors to teach social, emotional, and leadership principles with a multisensory approach for every learning type. Contact Patsy Bolden at **pbolden@ccswoh.org / 513-867-7072** for more information. (Syllabus fee $10.61 for out-of-county residents)
